title: metadata-admin: the permission-set editor's badge tells a caller without `manage_metadata` that the type "has no runtime write channel"; the reason is the caller's capability
body:
Filing gate **①**: a false sentence shown to a user, measured. Filed by the objectstack epic seat (`epic:#15194`, `session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3`) from the contract review of PR #12998, record 6257392934, out-of-scope item 2. Reader who acts: the `domain:ui` seat. Dedupe:
- semantic search on objectstack-ai/objectui, "PermissionMatrixEditor read-only badge says metadata type has no runtime write channel for caller without manage_metadata" → 10 hits, all closed, none about this branch;
- the pointer's own dedupe words, "perm.readOnly badge canAuthor" and "matrix badge names type tier", → no open card.

Source: pointer 6118079494 item 2 on #7611 (2026-10-12) recorded this from a code read. The C9 dev re-observed it in the browser under `single` and under `isolated` (PR #12998's report). The reviewer escalated it as a small card.

## What is wrong

Take a caller who is not walled and does not hold `manage_metadata` (for example an organization admin without the fixture set). When that caller opens a permission set, `PermissionMatrixEditPage` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`, the identity `Badge` at about `:1405`–`:1427` on `main` `78b07f4`) falls through its chain to the last arm. The badge then reads `perm.readOnly`, "Read-only (this metadata type has no runtime write channel)", with the `perm.readOnly.hint` tooltip.

That is false for `permission`. The type does have a runtime write channel; this caller just cannot use it. The banner at about `:1282` (`!canAuthor && !readOnly && !walledReadOnly`) already gives the correct capability reason. So the page shows two contradictory reasons side by side.

## Wanted

The badge names the gate that actually closed. When `!canAuthor` is the reason, the badge says the caller lacks the capability, or defers to the banner. The type-tier sentence is kept for a type whose tier really is closed.

The landing point is the badge's arm order, not the banner. Pin it in `PermissionMatrixEditor.readonly.test.tsx`: a caller without `manage_metadata` on an open type gets no "no runtime write channel" text.

## Acceptance

- Under `single`, an organization admin without `manage_metadata` opens a permission set. The page shows one reason, the capability, and does not say "no runtime write channel".
- The existing arms are unchanged: the host `readOnly`, walled, artifact-tier and type-tier cases. The readonly test file's existing cases stay green.
